title: Work
body:
**Work** is the transfer of energy by a force acting through a displacement.

$$
W = Fd\cos\theta
$$

where $\theta$ is the angle between the force and the displacement, which makes work the
[[Dot Product]] of the two vectors. It is a scalar measured in joules.

```
20 N pushing a box 5 m in the same direction:   W = 20 × 5 × cos 0° = 100 J
the same force at 60° to the motion:            W = 20 × 5 × cos 60° = 50 J
a force perpendicular to the motion:            W = 0
```

The last line has consequences. Carrying a box horizontally at constant speed does no work on
the box in this accounting, however tiring it is, because the upward force and the horizontal
displacement are perpendicular. The [[Tension]] holding a ball in
[[Uniform Circular Motion]] does no work either, which is why the speed stays
constant.

Work is negative when the force opposes the motion, which is how [[Friction]] removes energy
from a system.

For a force that varies with position, the product becomes an [[Integral]], $W = \int F\,dx$,
which is where the spring's $\frac{1}{2}kx^2$ comes from.
